column1: # derivation: §1.7: a WHEN whose condition is NULL is not taken; evaluation
# moves to the next WHEN, then to ELSE. r = CASE WHEN a THEN 1 WHEN b THEN 2
# ELSE 3: a TRUE (ids 1 to 3) gives 1; a FALSE or NULL with b TRUE (ids 4, 7)
# gives 2; otherwise 3 (ids 5, 6, 8, 9: b FALSE or NULL). r_not = CASE WHEN
# NOT a THEN 10 ELSE 20: NOT a is FALSE, TRUE, NULL for a TRUE, FALSE, NULL
# (§1.1), so a FALSE (ids 4 to 6) gives 10 and a TRUE or NULL gives 20.
# Types: every branch is an INT64 literal (§8.19), so the CASE is INT64;
# nullable: §8 declares nullable every result its table does not exempt.
